subject: RetailX live ingest failures - SDKWave connection dropouts
messages:
From: Tara Bloom <tara@retailx.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: RetailX EngOps <engops@retailx.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Live checkout ingest errors during peak (urgent)

Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp increase in checkout failures and backend timeouts on RetailX between 08:50-09:10 PT this morning. Error rate jumped from ~0.5% to ~7% and p99 latency for streaming responses spiked to >6s. Our side shows repeated connection resets from the SDKWave client during live ingest.

Attached is a small HAR and a short trace from our ingest worker (svc-trace-20260705.zip). We rolled some client-side retries and temporarily routed traffic to a legacy adapter which reduced errors, but this is impacting conversions.

Can you confirm whether this aligns with anything on your side? We are on SDKWave v2.3.1.

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Bloom
Head of Platform Ops, RetailX

Attachment: svc-trace-20260705.zip (trace)
Attachment: quick-har.log (partial request/response)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tara Bloom <tara@retailx.com>
Cc: RetailX EngOps <engops@retailx.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live checkout ingest errors during peak (urgent)

Thanks for the heads up, Tara — sorry for the impact. I'm escalating this to our on-call infra/SDK team immediately.

Quick asks while we investigate:
- Can you confirm whether the SDKWave clients are using the default header coalescing setting (coalesce=true)?
- Do you have a sample client request that reproduced the issue end-to-end (we already have the HAR + svc-trace).
- If possible, can you temporarily pin clients to v2.3.0 (our engineering team suspects a regression between 2.3.0 -> 2.3.1) and let us know whether that stops the dropouts?

We're triaging now and will provide an ETA for a mitigation.

— Soojin
Soovin (Soojin) Lee
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Tara Bloom <tara@retailx.com>, RetailX EngOps <engops@retailx.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live checkout ingest errors during peak (urgent)

Attaching an initial read of the svc-trace — thanks for sending. Observations:
- There are repeated "FRAME_DROP" events at the streaming parser boundary. The server-side ingest shows incomplete header frames (Content-Length present but body shorter than advertised).
- Error bursts line up with SDKWave v2.3.1 rollout windows in our rollout logs. We see increased connection resets from clients with the v2.3.1 user-agent.
- My hypothesis: a header coalescing change in SDKWave v2.3.1 causes the client to emit multi-part header blocks that our streaming parser assumed would always be coalesced into a single head. Under high concurrency, the parser sees a truncated header and drops the frame, causing retries and p99 spikes.

Short-term: force SDKWave clients to set coalesce=false (single-frame) or rollback to v2.3.0. I've prepared a small patch to the parser to tolerate split headers — attaching patch notes.

Attachment: debug-har.log
Attachment: RetailX_SDKWave_v2.3.1.patch.txt

— Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tara Bloom <tara@retailx.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live checkout ingest errors during peak (urgent)

Tara — quick update and temporary mitigation steps you can take now: 
1) If possible, pin SDKWave to v2.3.0 for the next 2 hours while we validate the parser patch. Our data shows that rollback eliminates the header-splitting pattern.
2) If rollback is not feasible, set SDKWave config headerCoalesce=false (single-frame) — this avoids the coalescing regression immediately.
3) We'll enable a fallback routing policy that sends RetailX traffic to a stable pool (this will add ~30–50ms latency but reduce error rate).

We're shipping an emergency parser patch to a canary pool this afternoon and will monitor. Expect a more formal postmortem once we have the patch validated.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll keep you updated every hour until resolved.

— Soojin
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: executive-team@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Executive brief: RetailX outage impact and recommended customer relief

Team — RetailX (RX-4492) experienced a material degradation during their peak window yesterday tied to our SDKWave v2.3.1 rollout. Impact: ~7% error rate for ~20 minutes during peak; they routed to legacy adapter which reduced but did not eliminate revenue impact.

We need to confirm the following by EOD:
- Customer-facing root cause statement and timeline
- Proposed customer remediation and credits (legal/sales to propose)
- ETA for full fix and whether we can accelerate a forced rollback for all customers on v2.3.1 if necessary

Soojin/Rishi — please prepare a 1-page exec summary for RetailX and recommended credit amount. Sales, please coordinate with RX account team.

— Jonas
VP, Customer Reliability
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Postmortem snapshot & next steps — RetailX SDKWave issue

Summary (internal):
- Incident window: 2026-07-05 08:50–09:10 PT. Root cause: header coalescing change in SDKWave v2.3.1 combined with a parser assumption that headers arrive fully coalesced. Under high concurrency, split header blocks caused FRAME_DROP and connection resets.
- Immediate customer actions taken: temporary routing to legacy adapter, recommended rollback to v2.3.0 / headerCoalesce=false. RetailX applied rollback and reported error rate back to baseline.
- Engineering mitigations: 1) Emergency parser patch (handle fragmented header blocks) deployed to canary at 2026-07-06 15:30 PT; 2) Full rollout targeted for 2026-07-07 18:00 PT after load testing; 3) E2E test added to SDK compatibility suite to detect coalescing regressions.
- Customer comms: drafting a root cause note and remediation timeline for RetailX; recommend a service credit covering the 20-minute peak window plus goodwill credit.

Action items (owners):
- Rishi: finalize parser patch, run full soak, prepare rollout plan (ETA: EOD 2026-07-07)
- Marissa: coordinate customer credit proposal with Sales/Finance (ETA: EOD 2026-07-07)
- Soojin: finalize RetailX-facing timeline and send root cause note (ETA: 2026-07-07 14:00 PT)

We will keep this thread open until the patch is fully rolled out and RetailX signs off.

— Soojin
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
summary: Customer reports intermittent connection dropouts and p99 latency spikes during peak checkout window. Root cause linked to SDKWave v2.3.1 header coalescing regression causing truncated streaming frames. Short-term mitigations: force single-frame mode, rollback to v2.3.0, routing to fallback model. Long-term: patch parser to handle fragmented headers and add e2e test harness.
